Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25 15:00 UTC

Recording: Fireflies auto-record
Links shared: https://redwood.example.com/co-sell-one-pager (deck), /sprint/integ-checklist.xlsx

Summary (auto): Quick handoff from AE -> SE, align on pilot success criteria and decide hosted vs dedicated for pilot. Legal raised a couple procurement/questions about data residency and vendor questionnaire.

[00:00] Jordan Ellis (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm Jordan with Redwood, i'll kick us off, we have priya on the se side and marcus on csm... uh Marcus, you wanna say hi?
[00:05] Marcus Li (CSM): Hey all, Marcus here, excited to get this moving.
[00:08] Ava Gonzalez (Silverpine): Hi, Ava. Thanks for doing this — Silverpine excited to explore co-sell.
[00:12] Ben Hsu (Silverpine): Ben here, i'll own the joint outreach bits.
[00:15] Jordan: Quick agenda — 1) handoff/context 2) technical assumptions 3) security and procurement 4) pilot success metrics and go/no-go 5) next steps. Sound good?
[00:21] Ava: yep

[00:40] Priya Nair (SE): Cool, i'm Priya. Tech quick context — Silverpine said they want an in-product LLM assistant for data discovery and a reranking endpoint for their search. We're proposing a co-sell pilot that bundles Redwood hosted inference for the MVP but with an option to move to Dedicated or Private if the enterprise customers require VPC/HSM.
[00:55] Ben: correct — some of our enterprise customers push for VPC or private deploy so we need those options surfaced.
[01:05] Priya: Totally. For pilot we typically recommend hosted to get velocity, but we can do dedicated capacity for predictable latency if you want to lock it. Also we have caching and batching that can drop token cost substantially — but that can affect tail latency so that's a tradeoff.

[04:00] Ava: can you give us ballpark numbers — latency SLOs and cost per 1M tokens for hosted vs dedicated?
[04:12] Priya: rough numbers: hosted avg p99 for short prompts ~190-250ms depending on model, dedicated with pinned GPU ~110-160ms p99; cost directionally 20-40% higher for dedicated in committed scenarios but you get stable throughput. i'll send a spreadsheet. (slight stutter) those are ballparks, final depends on sequence length and model.
[05:00] Ben: ok that helps. for our pitch we need a slide showing run-rate economics — like 10k users, avg 15k tokens/day.

[06:20] Jordan: on the GTM, we propose a revenue share — Redwood typically does a co-sell referral fee for FY24/25 pilots, we can propose 10-15% on net new ARR. that'll be in the one-pager.
[06:40] Ava: we'll need to see the agreement language. our legal will want audit logs and SOC 2 evidence.

[09:10] Marta Ribeiro (Legal): hi Marta — quick note from legal: vendor questionnaire is attached, we need answers on encryption at rest, KMS/HSM, key rotation, and ability to restrict data residency to eu-west for a subset of customers. also SSO/SAML and RBAC compliance.
[09:35] Priya: on encryption — Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM in Private deployments; hosted supports encryption at rest and in transit but CMKs are available on Dedicated/Private. we'll call out the specifics in the security doc.
[10:05] Marta: great, can you flag which items are only available on Private vs Dedicated vs Hosted? that will speed procurement.
[10:20] Priya: yes — we'll produce a matrix.

[12:00] Jordan: timeline question — when are you looking to pilot?
[12:08] Ava: Q2 this year, ideally pilot kick off early April and run 6-8 weeks.
[12:15] Jordan: ok that's workable. for a hosted pilot we can be faster — dedicated or private adds about 2-3 weeks for capacity/provisioning.

[15:40] Priya: technical constraints: what stack are you integrating with? are you sending full PII payloads? where are logs stored?
[15:50] Ava: our platform is on GCP in eu-west, we use BigQuery for analytics and we typically send semistructured payloads — PII is redacted upstream but some customers may want no logging.
[16:05] Priya: for no-logging we can enable no-persistent-logs mode on private/dedicated and redact at the client layer; hosted supports retention controls but full no-logs usually requires Dedicated/Private and contractual SLAs.

[18:00] Ben: any SDKs or connectors? we want a quick integration pattern for our product team.
[18:10] Priya: REST + SDKs (python/js), there's a sample connector for BigQuery export -> Redwood ingest we'll share. also a webhook pattern for re-ranking.

[22:30] Jordan: ok let's talk pilot success metrics — Ava what would make this a success from Silverpine's perspective?
[22:40] Ava: measurable revenue enablement — two named accounts convert to paid plans, latency p95 <300ms for primary flows, per-request cost below our threshold to keep LTV economics valid. also customer satisfaction > 8 NPS on the pilot cohort.
[23:05] Priya: we'll align instrumentation — token usage, latency histograms, error rates, and a quality eval set for hallucination/regression. Redwood Optimize can run prompt/quantization suggestions to reduce cost without significant quality loss.

[27:00] Marta: procurement — we have a standard vendor contract; who at Redwood will be legal touch?
[27:10] Jordan: i'll loop in our legal lead, and Marcus will be the CSM for contract execution. we'll also surface a redlines doc.

[30:00] (brief cross talk)
[30:30] Priya: one technical caveat — if you enable continuous batching to save cost, tail latency can increase under burst. For customer-facing search we recommend a dedicated path for low-latency re-ranking and batch for offline generation.
[31:00] Ben: noted. so maybe mix modes per route.

[35:15] Ava: any red flags around data residency? Some of our telco customers require EU-only processing.
[35:25] Priya: we can route requests to eu-west region; for guarantee of data residency we usually use Private or a Dedicated pool in the region with contractual commitments. we'll call out fallbacks if eu capacity is saturated.

[39:00] Jordan: competitors — who else are you evaluating?
[39:05] Ava: Databricks for embeddings and search, and Pinecone for vector infra, but they don't do the end-to-end inference bundling the way you do. Also we've looked at Anthropic for LLM.
[39:20] Jordan: good to know. we'll emphasize our unified runtime + cost controls.

[42:40] Priya: on instrumentation — we will provide a dashboard (console link to be shared) with token-level cost, per-route latency, trace ids to tie to your logs, and errors. we'll also include a lightweight eval harness to catch regressions.

[47:00] Marta: we need to see SOC 2 report and pen test summary before we go into any contract.
[47:10] Jordan: absolutely — i'll attach our SOC 2 report and a short security pack in the follow-up.

[51:20] Ben: for co-sell activities — can we get co-branded one-pager and an email template?
[51:30] Jordan: yes — i'll include a co-branded 1-pager and a joint email cadence doc.

[55:00] Priya: next on the technical checklist: 1) confirm model (we recommend open model X or Redwood-curated variant), 2) sample payloads for baseline, 3) define routes (search/rerank vs assistant), 4) logging/retention mode.
[55:20] Ava: we'll deliver sample payloads and a short customer list.

[59:40] (brief pause, background noise)
[60:00] Jordan: recap — Jordan sends one-pager + pricing + SOC2; Priya sends integration checklist + sample SDKs + baseline template; Marcus proposes pilot kickoff times; Ava sends pilot customer list + vendor questionnaire redlines.
[60:22] Ava: sounds great.
[61:00] Marta: i'll get redlines back by april 1.
[61:10] Priya: We'll also flag which features require Dedicated/Private so procurement isn't surprised.
[61:25] Ben: i'll prep the GTM motion with target accounts and share by friday.

[70:00] Jordan: Any other questions?
[70:10] Ava: none here, thank you.
[70:15] Jordan: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with notes and docs.

[72:00] End of recording
